title: Reported Speech Quiz 5
description: Every question hides a trap: a present reporting verb, a conditional, a modal that stays or a double reading.
instructions: Use the standard rule: the reporting verb is in the past and the situation is over, unless a question says otherwise.
Every question has a trap. Read every word.

questions.question: Report this: 'I have been waiting for an hour,' she said.
options: she has been waiting for an hour.
she had waiting for an hour.
she had been waiting for an hour.
she would be waiting for an hour.
questions.explanation: The present perfect continuous becomes the past perfect continuous. Watch out: would be waiting changes the meaning to the future.

questions.question: 'The teacher said the earth goes round the sun' is correct, because a general truth need not be backshifted.
questions.explanation: A fact that is always true can keep the present tense. Watch out: this is the exception to the backshift rule.

questions.question: 'If I see her, I will tell her,' he said. → He said that if he {{1}} her, he {{2}} tell her.
questions.explanation: The first conditional moves one step back: see becomes saw and will becomes would. Watch out: both verbs move.

questions.question: 'If I were rich, I would travel,' she said. → She said that if she ___ rich, she would travel.
options: were
had been
would be
is
questions.explanation: The second conditional does not change: were. Watch out: had been is the third conditional.

questions.question: 'You should rest,' she said. → She told me that I ___ rest.
options: would
had to
must
should
questions.explanation: Should is already a backshifted form, so it does not change. Watch out: had to would turn advice into an obligation.

questions.question: Correct the mistake: He told he would come the next day.
accepted: He said he would come the next day.
He said he would come the next day
He told me he would come the next day.
He told me he would come the next day
He told her he would come the next day.
He told her he would come the next day
He told us he would come the next day.
He told us he would come the next day
He told them he would come the next day.
He told them he would come the next day
questions.explanation: Told needs a person: He told me he would come, or he said he would come. Watch out: tell without a person is always wrong.

questions.assertion: 'Tomorrow' usually becomes 'the next day' when the report is made later.
questions.reason: Time words are measured from the moment of speaking, which is now in the past.
questions.explanation: Both statements are true, and the reason explains the assertion: time words are measured from the speaking moment, which is now in the past. Watch out: if the report is made on the same day, tomorrow can stay.

questions.question: 'I saw him last week,' she said. → She said she {{1}} him the week before.
questions.explanation: The past simple becomes the past perfect, and last week becomes the week before. Watch out: both changes are needed.

questions.question: Which sentences are correct?
options: He told me that he had lost his keys.
She asked if I could help her.
He said me that he was ill.
She asked me where was the station.
questions.explanation: The correct reports use told + person and statement order. Watch out: said me and where was keep the original structure.

questions.question: Put the words in the correct order.
questions.explanation: The reporting clause, then the clause with had finished, then the time phrase. Watch out: the day before goes last.

questions.question: Report this: 'Don't touch it!' he shouted.
options: He warned me don't touch it.
He warned me not to touch it.
He suggested me not to touch it.
He warned that I not touch it.
questions.explanation: Warn + person + not to + verb. Watch out: the imperative cannot stay, and suggested me to is wrong.

questions.question: 'He said he had been there' can report either 'I was there' or 'I have been there'.
questions.explanation: Both the past simple and the present perfect become the past perfect. Watch out: the report alone cannot tell you which one was said.
